title: Change of rings preserves K-flat complexes with flat terms
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\varphi:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O'$ a morphism of sheaves of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Let $\mathcal K^\bullet$ be a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex] whose terms $\mathcal K^p$ are flat $\mathcal O$-modules (the functor $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal K^p$ on $\mathcal O$-modules is exact). Then the complex $\mathcal K^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$, obtained by applying the change of rings $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] termwise, is a K-flat complex of $\mathcal O'$-modules whose terms are flat $\mathcal O'$-modules.

source.place: Lemma 21.18.1, Tag 0G7E (sites-cohomology-lemma-pullback-K-flat), for the morphism of ringed topoi $(\Sh(\mathcal C),\mathcal O')\to(\Sh(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ given by the identity of $\Sh(\mathcal C)$ and $\varphi$, whose pullback $f^*$ is $-\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal O'$

proof.text: Write $R=\mathcal O$, $S=\mathcal O\prime$, and $U=\varphi_*$ for restriction of scalars. This leaves the underlying abelian sheaf and maps unchanged. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels in both module categories, so their underlying abelian sheaves agree before and after $U$. Thus $U$ preserves and reflects exactness, and for every complex $F$ the underlying abelian sheaves of $H^i(UF)$ and $H^i(F)$ coincide; in particular $U$ preserves and reflects acyclicity.

source.place: Tag 03DA, label lemma-abelian; kernel and cokernel descriptions immediately preceding the lemma

proof.text: Apply the natural tensor cancellation theorem [lem-pur-change-of-rings-tensor-cancellation]. It constructs U(N tensor_S (M tensor_R S)) ≅ UN tensor_R M, natural in both variables, directly from the sectionwise balanced equivalence and monoidal sheafification. No bilinear-extension theorem is needed.

source.place: Section 03EK, tensor product and its bilinear universal property; Tag 05V4, label lemma-flat-change-of-rings, displayed tensor identity

proof.text: Fix p and write TR = - tensor_R K^p and TS = - tensor_S E(K^p). Step 2 and the identity law for changeOfRingsHom give a natural isomorphism TS followed by U ≅ U followed by TR. The right-hand composite preserves finite limits and finite colimits by the flatness hypothesis and step 1. Restriction is conservative and preserves finite limits and colimits, so it reflects them. Transport along the natural isomorphism and reflection prove exactness of TS.

source.place: Tag 05V4, label lemma-flat-change-of-rings, proof with the module denoted H on the left also on the right

proof.text: Restriction of scalars preserves the coproducts used in totalization: composing it with the conservative underlying-abelian-sheaf functor is the underlying-abelian-sheaf functor over S, and that functor preserves these coproducts. Apply the isomorphisms of step 2 in each bidegree. Their naturality in the second variable gives compatibility with the vertical differential, and their naturality in the first variable gives compatibility with the horizontal differential. They therefore give a bicomplex isomorphism. The additive mapTotalIso comparison and totalization of this bicomplex isomorphism identify U Tot(F tensor_S E(K)) with Tot(UF tensor_R K), including the standard total-complex signs.

source.place: Tag 06YL, tensor totalization preceding Definition 06YN; sites-modules Tag 03DB, label lemma-limits-colimits, direct-sum construction

proof.text: Now let $F$ be any acyclic complex of $S$-module sheaves. Step 1 makes $UF$ acyclic. By K-flatness of $K$, the complex $\operatorname{Tot}(UF\otimes_R K)$ is acyclic. The chain isomorphism of step 4 and reflection of acyclicity in step 1 make $\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_S(K\otimes_R S))$ acyclic. This is precisely the definition of K-flatness over $S$. Together with step 3 it proves both conclusions.
